170d1ae080 Kenneth Jiang 2026-10-19 18:19:35 -0700
Add Anthropic and OpenRouter as Agent providers behind one provider-neutral turn loop

The in-app Agent talked to one API, OpenAI's Responses API, through
OpenAIResponsesAgent, which mixed the tool-call turn loop with that
wire format and with OpenAI-specific choices. Adding a second provider
would have meant a second copy of the loop.

ProviderAgent now owns the loop and a provider-neutral transcript: the
instructions, the tools offered, the earlier conversation, this turn's
user content, and one step per response holding the provider's own
record of its reply (kept verbatim, because both OpenAI and Anthropic
want it echoed back unchanged) with the results of the calls it made.
Every rule the old class enforced is unchanged: calls run one at a time
in the order written, a failed call answers the rest unrun, unknown or
invalid calls are refused back at most twice a turn, images follow
results, fired skills are sent once on OpenAI, and late events from a
cancelled request are dropped.

A codec per API family turns that transcript into a request and each
streamed payload into neutral events. ResponsesCodec serves OpenAI and
OpenRouter; its request bodies are byte-identical to the old adapter's,
checked against the shell harness's recorded bodies. AnthropicCodec
serves the Messages API: system and tool cache breakpoints, tool_use and
tool_result replay, same-role merging, images inside tool results, call
arguments assembled from streamed fragments, every stop reason mapped,
and the keywords Anthropic's strict mode rejects (minimum, maximum,
minLength, maxLength, maxItems) moved from each tool's schema into the
property description, so the registry keeps its full schemas for native
validation and for MCP clients. On Anthropic a fired skill stays in place
on later requests of the same turn, because dropping it counts as editing
history and Opus 5.5 then rejects replayed thinking.

Providers are data in ProviderProfile: family, endpoint, auth header,
fixed headers, default model, output limit and display name. OpenRouter
defaults to the same model as OpenAI; Anthropic to claude-opus-5-5 with
a 64000-token output limit. Setup and configuration build the agent
through one factory keyed by provider, and JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT
overrides whichever endpoint is active (JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT still
works). The setup page offers OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic, with
OpenAI still the default tab. OpenAIResponsesAgent remains as a thin
subclass so the harness compiles unchanged.

Tests: the adapter tests are split into loop tests driven through a
scripted fake codec and wire tests per codec; a conformance test drives
one scripted turn through both codecs and requires identical events;
unit tests cover the schema projection. test_provider_live.cpp holds
metered live smokes that skip without a key and refuse any request that
could cross a $0.50 cap. Their first runs are recorded there: OpenRouter,
4 requests, $0.0107; Anthropic, 7 requests, $0.0886, including the
history check with a fired skill, OpenAI-minted call ids in replayed
history, and both title-request shapes.

The tool registry, ToolExecutionCoordinator, AgentHost and the MCP
server are unchanged.

170d1ae080 Kenneth Jiang 2026-10-19 18:19:35 -0700
Add Anthropic and OpenRouter as Agent providers behind one provider-neutral turn loop

The in-app Agent talked to one API, OpenAI's Responses API, through
OpenAIResponsesAgent, which mixed the tool-call turn loop with that
wire format and with OpenAI-specific choices. Adding a second provider
would have meant a second copy of the loop.

ProviderAgent now owns the loop and a provider-neutral transcript: the
instructions, the tools offered, the earlier conversation, this turn's
user content, and one step per response holding the provider's own
record of its reply (kept verbatim, because both OpenAI and Anthropic
want it echoed back unchanged) with the results of the calls it made.
Every rule the old class enforced is unchanged: calls run one at a time
in the order written, a failed call answers the rest unrun, unknown or
invalid calls are refused back at most twice a turn, images follow
results, fired skills are sent once on OpenAI, and late events from a
cancelled request are dropped.

A codec per API family turns that transcript into a request and each
streamed payload into neutral events. ResponsesCodec serves OpenAI and
OpenRouter; its request bodies are byte-identical to the old adapter's,
checked against the shell harness's recorded bodies. AnthropicCodec
serves the Messages API: system and tool cache breakpoints, tool_use and
tool_result replay, same-role merging, images inside tool results, call
arguments assembled from streamed fragments, every stop reason mapped,
and the keywords Anthropic's strict mode rejects (minimum, maximum,
minLength, maxLength, maxItems) moved from each tool's schema into the
property description, so the registry keeps its full schemas for native
validation and for MCP clients. On Anthropic a fired skill stays in place
on later requests of the same turn, because dropping it counts as editing
history and Opus 5.5 then rejects replayed thinking.

Providers are data in ProviderProfile: family, endpoint, auth header,
fixed headers, default model, output limit and display name. OpenRouter
defaults to the same model as OpenAI; Anthropic to claude-opus-5-5 with
a 64000-token output limit. Setup and configuration build the agent
through one factory keyed by provider, and JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT
overrides whichever endpoint is active (JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT still
works). The setup page offers OpenAI, OpenRouter and Anthropic, with
OpenAI still the default tab. OpenAIResponsesAgent remains as a thin
subclass so the harness compiles unchanged.

Tests: the adapter tests are split into loop tests driven through a
scripted fake codec and wire tests per codec; a conformance test drives
one scripted turn through both codecs and requires identical events;
unit tests cover the schema projection. test_provider_live.cpp holds
metered live smokes that skip without a key and refuse any request that
could cross a $0.50 cap. Their first runs are recorded there: OpenRouter,
4 requests, $0.0107; Anthropic, 7 requests, $0.0886, including the
history check with a fired skill, OpenAI-minted call ids in replayed
history, and both title-request shapes.

The tool registry, ToolExecutionCoordinator, AgentHost and the MCP
server are unchanged.

content.content:
=== 334287e2d8 Store intent and plan on each chat; show the plan headline on the setup card
Each chat now owns its print intent, purpose setup and plan. The project's
current ones are the active chat's, read through activeConversationId and
stored nowhere else. A new chat, and the replacement made when the active
chat is deleted, starts with a copy of the active chat's intent and no plan.
Resuming a chat makes it active and restores its model version; its intent
and plan never left it. A chat checkpoint keeps only the model version, the
boundary, the time and the card summary; the saved card reads its title and
headline from its own chat.

Region annotations belong with the model. Saved model versions held no
project-document state at all (restore always kept the current document, so
the old header comment about taking the earlier version's intent and plan was
wrong). Each version manifest now records the document's region list when it
is saved, a change to that list counts as a new version, and restoring or
resuming a version puts its list back.

The project-state schema is reset to version 1 with no migration, because
the project is not live yet: a document of any other version loads as a
fresh one, like a corrupt one. The older-record reads go with it (activity
source guessed from the correlation id, numbered default titles, the
skeleton merge and viewed-chat backfill), as do the version store's
first-format HEAD, the version-1 current-state wrapper and per-version
state.json reads. Project-state files saved during development load as fresh
documents and lose their chats.

The setup card shows the plan's headline in place of the preset-difference
rows, in every card state, and no line when there is no plan. The
"N objects with overrides" note stays on its own line. plan_set pushes the
card's context when it succeeds. The detailed setup page keeps every
difference, in OrcaSlicer's own preset/page/group order. Removed: the card's
difference selection, ranking, "more changes" count and "No changes from
presets" line, and the agent-authorship layer (remembering patch results,
replaying activities, binding to presets, the two maps).

Two intentional changes to the model's input, both in the re-recorded
tests/project_prompt/requests.json:
- preset differences no longer carry "origin";
- the in-app agent's own edits no longer mark its plan needs_reassessment.
  A person's edit (Undo and Redo included), an external MCP client's edit
  and a version restore still do. The recording's 240 needs_reassessment
  values are now current.
A third: a new chat's model sees no plan until it calls plan_set; before,
it inherited the previous chat's. plan_set's description now asks for a
short strategy headline (about 8 to 12 words) and a refresh when the
strategy changes.

=== 57b58cb268 Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record
The setup card's title (what the person wants) and its headline (how the
agent will print it) were written by two tools, and the model kept them apart
badly: in batch B's changed-strategy journeys (2026-10-19) it rewrote the
headline with plan_set but never called intent_update, so the card read
"dried flowers, spiral vase" above "watertight multi-wall". The two records
were already handled as one (same coordinator block, both in-app only, both
on the chat, the same context push), so they are now one tool.

setup_record takes, all at the top level:
- purpose, required on every call, at most 60 characters: what the person
  wants the print to be or do, in a few words and their terms, not how to
  print it (no settings, material, printer or print mode unless the person
  made one of them the goal). It titles the setup card.
- fields, optional, with intent_update's semantics (assumed, question,
  provenance).
- headline, decisions, unverified, risks: the plan, optional. With a
  headline they replace the whole plan; with none the plan is kept, so a
  purpose can be recorded before there is a strategy. unverified is one
  sentence per thing taken as true without being able to check.
The result carries the intent section, purposeChange and the setup in force,
and always the plan as it now stands. The card's context is pushed once per
successful call, so title and headline arrive together.

The setup-changed skill fires on a first purpose or changed fields, as
before; a new purpose wording alone is title_only, and a call that only
restates the purpose to change the plan is unchanged, so neither fires it.

Why it looks like this (DeepSeek V4 Flash, live runs of 2026-10-19/20):
- "purpose", not "setupTitle": under either tool 7 of 12 batch-B titles,
  and some batch-C titles, described the setup ("Rhino figurine — 0.16mm,
  3 walls, organic supports"); with the rename and the description every
  title in two later batches was goal-only.
- A flat plan, not a nested object: the model sent the nested plan as a
  string of JSON, which the registry refuses; two refusals end a turn.
- "unverified", not "assumptions": next to fields' "assumed" flag, the
  model put intent-field objects under assumptions. This last rename has
  not been run live.

Changes to the model's input: one tool where there were two (27 project
tools), "purpose" and "unverified" in each turn's <workspace> block and in
tool results (including workspace_inspect's plan section), the project
prompt's line "the print's purpose recorded with setup_record, a setup that
suits it, checked, ...", and the setup-changed skill's "record the plan,
with what is unverified, using setup_record first".

Rebased onto jusprin-newui 5ca13e4234. intent_update's rule from 3341abf38f,
never record a purpose the person has not stated, even marked assumed, is
carried into purpose's description; with purpose required on every call, a
plan cannot be recorded before the person states a purpose. The <workspace>
block is now built in ProviderAgent.cpp, which takes the purpose and
unverified renames. test_provider_agent, test_anthropic_codec and
test_provider_live count 27 tools and call setup_record.

On the Claude subscription (claude-cli backend and judge, Opus 5.5, all 24
cases three times each, 2026-10-20): 70 passed, 2 failed, none unobserved,
against the subscription baseline's 69, 3, 0. The two failures are
print-this-no-purpose asking two questions, as in that baseline.

=== 57b58cb268 Merge intent_update and plan_set into one tool, setup_record
The setup card's title (what the person wants) and its headline (how the
agent will print it) were written by two tools, and the model kept them apart
badly: in batch B's changed-strategy journeys (2026-10-19) it rewrote the
headline with plan_set but never called intent_update, so the card read
"dried flowers, spiral vase" above "watertight multi-wall". The two records
were already handled as one (same coordinator block, both in-app only, both
on the chat, the same context push), so they are now one tool.

setup_record takes, all at the top level:
- purpose, required on every call, at most 60 characters: what the person
  wants the print to be or do, in a few words and their terms, not how to
  print it (no settings, material, printer or print mode unless the person
  made one of them the goal). It titles the setup card.
- fields, optional, with intent_update's semantics (assumed, question,
  provenance).
- headline, decisions, unverified, risks: the plan, optional. With a
  headline they replace the whole plan; with none the plan is kept, so a
  purpose can be recorded before there is a strategy. unverified is one
  sentence per thing taken as true without being able to check.
The result carries the intent section, purposeChange and the setup in force,
and always the plan as it now stands. The card's context is pushed once per
successful call, so title and headline arrive together.

The setup-changed skill fires on a first purpose or changed fields, as
before; a new purpose wording alone is title_only, and a call that only
restates the purpose to change the plan is unchanged, so neither fires it.

Why it looks like this (DeepSeek V4 Flash, live runs of 2026-10-19/20):
- "purpose", not "setupTitle": under either tool 7 of 12 batch-B titles,
  and some batch-C titles, described the setup ("Rhino figurine — 0.16mm,
  3 walls, organic supports"); with the rename and the description every
  title in two later batches was goal-only.
- A flat plan, not a nested object: the model sent the nested plan as a
  string of JSON, which the registry refuses; two refusals end a turn.
- "unverified", not "assumptions": next to fields' "assumed" flag, the
  model put intent-field objects under assumptions. This last rename has
  not been run live.

Changes to the model's input: one tool where there were two (27 project
tools), "purpose" and "unverified" in each turn's <workspace> block and in
tool results (including workspace_inspect's plan section), the project
prompt's line "the print's purpose recorded with setup_record, a setup that
suits it, checked, ...", and the setup-changed skill's "record the plan,
with what is unverified, using setup_record first".

Rebased onto jusprin-newui 5ca13e4234. intent_update's rule from 3341abf38f,
never record a purpose the person has not stated, even marked assumed, is
carried into purpose's description; with purpose required on every call, a
plan cannot be recorded before the person states a purpose. The <workspace>
block is now built in ProviderAgent.cpp, which takes the purpose and
unverified renames. test_provider_agent, test_anthropic_codec and
test_provider_live count 27 tools and call setup_record.

On the Claude subscription (claude-cli backend and judge, Opus 5.5, all 24
cases three times each, 2026-10-20): 70 passed, 2 failed, none unobserved,
against the subscription baseline's 69, 3, 0. The two failures are
print-this-no-purpose asking two questions, as in that baseline.

tests/project_prompt: prepare-petg-strong also fails a setup_record whose
purpose says how to print (SETUP_WORDS); grading, script, README,
project_tools.json and requests.json updated and re-recorded with the
scripted model.

Two new commits landed on `jusprin-newui`: the setup-card work, rebased onto today's commits. They resolve the `setup_record` overlap I flagged. None of the other open items is addressed. Nothing is pushed; `origin` has nothing newer.

- **57b58cb268** merges `intent_update` and `plan_set` into one tool, `setup_record`.

What I checked in the tree, beyond the commit messages:
- **The "don't record a guessed purpose" rule carried over.** `setup_record`'s description says: "Record only a purpose the person stated, never one they have not, even marked assumed: ask them first."
- **The tool list was regenerated.** `project_tools.json` now has 27 tools, with `setup_record` and without `intent_update` or `plan_set`.

**One loose end:** the merge commit says it re-ran the suite on the subscription after the tool change and got **70 passed, 2 failed, 0 unobserved**. The two failures are `print-this-no-purpose` asking two questions, as before. But the README's subscription baseline table still shows today's 69/3/0, from before the tool list changed. class Step:
    """What the model did with the request: its reply, or the tool call that
    stands for its calls. A response may hold several calls, and the app runs
    every one, so a change among them is the step whatever came before it
    (the first change, if several); a response of reads is the first read,
    and each_read() gives a step for every read. Every call is in the report."""

    def __init__(self, output, index=None):
        self.output = output
        self.calls = [item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
        self.reply = "".join(output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message").strip()
        if index is None:
            index = next((i for i, item in enumerate(self.calls) if item.get("name") not in READS), 0)
        self.index = index
        call = self.calls[index] if self.calls else None
        self.tool = call["name"] if call else None
        self.call_id = call.get("call_id") if call else None
        self.arguments = self.parsed(call) if call else {}
        self.problem = self.invalid() if call else ""

    @staticmethod
    def parsed(call):
        try:
            return json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return {"(unreadable)": call.get("arguments")}

    def each_read(self):
        """A step for every call of a response with no change in it, in the
        order the model wrote them."""
        return [Step(self.output, index) for index in range(len(self.calls))]

    def invalid(self):
        """Arguments the registry would refuse, as far as the schema says. The
        refusal is not this suite's to test; it is reported beside the call."""
        schema = next((tool["parameters"] for tool in TOOLS if tool["name"] == self.tool), None)
        if schema is None:
            return "unknown tool"
        missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in self.arguments]
        extra = [name for name in self.arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
        return f"invalid arguments: missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}" if missing or extra else ""

    def keys(self):
        """The settings a settings call names."""
        return set(self.arguments.get("keys") or []) | set(self.arguments.get("changes") or {})

    def changes(self):
        return self.tool is not None and self.tool not in READS

    def reads(self):
        return self.tool in READS

    def __str__(self):
        if not self.tool:
            return "reply: " + (self.reply.replace("\n", " ")[:160] or "(empty)")
        text = f"{self.tool} {json.dumps(self.arguments, ensure_ascii=False)}" + (f" ({self.problem})" if self.problem else "")
        others = [f"{call['name']} {json.dumps(self.parsed(call), ensure_ascii=False)}"
                  for index, call in enumerate(self.calls) if index != self.index]
        return text + (f" [same response: {'; '.join(others)}]" if others else "")


# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each case names its request in requests.json and, in its docstring, the
# sentence of projectInstructions.ts it tests (line numbers at 6b4b8b6188).
# check() returns PASS, FAIL, UNOBSERVED or CONTINUE with a detail. CONTINUE
# is a read the case does not decide on: when it decides on none of a
# response's reads, the runner answers them all from the recording and asks
# again. UNOBSERVED is a step the case can say nothing about, or a read with
# no recorded answer, or the model still reading after MAX_READS answers.


def run_steps(name, respond, deliver=lambda step, results: None):
    """One run of a case: respond(input) is the model's output for the
    request so far, deliver(step, results) hands it its reads' results."""
    input = list(REQUESTS[name]["body"]["input"])
    # The recorded request's last items that the app sends on it alone (a
    # skill and its picture): a continuation of the turn leaves them out.
    once = REQUESTS[name].get("once", 0)
    path = []  # the reads answered, one entry per response, for the report
    try:
        for _ in range(MAX_READS + 1):
            log = [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]
            step = Step(respond(input))
            verdict, detail = judge_response(CASES[name](REQUESTS[name], log), step)
            if verdict != CONTINUE:
                break
            results, missing = answers_for(name, step)
            if results is None or len(path) == MAX_READS:
                verdict = UNOBSERVED
                detail = (f"no recorded answer for {missing}" if results is None else f"still reading after answers: {step}")
                break
            path.append(" + ".join(call["name"] for call in step.calls))
            deliver(step, results)
            # As the app continues a turn: the history without what was sent
            # once, the model's output, then a result for every call, in the
            # order the calls were written.
            if once:
                del input[-once:]
                once = 0
            input += step.output + [{"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call.get("call_id"), "output": result}
                                    for call, result in zip(step.calls, results)]
    except Exception as error:  # a failed request is a failed run, reported as such
        return FAIL, f"ERROR {error}", [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]
    prefix = f"after {', '.join(path)}: " if path else ""
    return verdict, prefix + detail, log + ["model: " + str(step)] + (["model said: " + step.reply] if step.reply and step.tool else [])


def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", choices=sorted(CASES), help="run only this case (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, help=f"runs per case (default: {RUN_BUDGET} shared by the cases run, "
                                                 f"at most {MAX_RUNS} each)")
    parser.add_argument("--must-pass", type=int, help="runs per case that must pass (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, help="runs in parallel, across cases (default 5; 3 for claude-cli)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", help=f"the model under test (default {MODEL})")
    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", help=f"its Responses API endpoint (default {ENDPOINT})")
    parser.add_argument("--key-env", help=f"environment variable holding that endpoint's key (default {KEY_ENV})")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", action="append",
                        help="OpenRouter only: serve every request from this host (repeatable, in order of preference; "
                             f"default for {MODEL}: {', '.join(PROVIDERS)})")
    parser.add_argument("--backend", choices=("api", "claude-cli"), default="api",
                        help="api: the model over its Responses API (default); claude-cli: the local Claude Code CLI "
                             "on the developer's Claude subscription")
    parser.add_argument("--claude-model", default=CLAUDE_MODEL, help=f"claude-cli's model (default {CLAUDE_MODEL})")
    parser.add_argument("--claude-effort", default=CLAUDE_EFFORT, help=f"claude-cli's effort (default {CLAUDE_EFFORT})")
    parser.add_argument("--judge", choices=("openai", "claude-cli"), default="openai",
                        help=f"openai: {JUDGE_MODEL} (default, the baselines' judge); claude-cli: the local Claude Code "
                             "CLI. Changing the judge starts a new baseline")
    parser.add_argument("--claude-judge-model", default=CLAUDE_MODEL,
                        help=f"the claude-cli judge's model (default {CLAUDE_MODEL})")
    parser.add_argument("--claude-keep", metavar="DIR",
                        help="claude-cli: keep each run's session, tools, MCP config and CLI stream under DIR")
    parser.add_argument("--prompt-rev", metavar="REV",
                        help="run the prompt as the page's source had it at this git revision (6b4b8b6188 or later)")
    parser.add_argument("--render-only", action="store_true", help="print the request bodies and their sizes; send nothing")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every run's conversation, not only failures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    global CLAUDE_JUDGE
    if args.judge == "claude-cli":
        CLAUDE_JUDGE = (args.claude_judge_model, args.claude_effort)
    if args.jobs is None:
        args.jobs = 3 if args.backend == "claude-cli" else 5
    model, endpoint, key_env = args.model or MODEL, args.endpoint or ENDPOINT, args.key_env or KEY_ENV
    providers = args.provider or (PROVIDERS if model == MODEL else None)
    names = args.case or list(CASES)
    if args.runs is None:
        args.runs = max(1, min(MAX_RUNS, RUN_BUDGET // len(names)))
    instructions = render(args.prompt_rev)

    if args.render_only:

class Step:
    """What the model did with the request: its reply, or the tool call that
    stands for its calls. A response may hold several calls, and the app runs
    every one, so a change among them is the step whatever came before it
    (the first change, if several); a response of reads is the first read,
    and each_read() gives a step for every read. Every call is in the report."""

    def __init__(self, output, index=None):
        self.output = output
        self.calls = [item for item in output if item.get("type") == "function_call"]
        self.reply = "".join(output_text(item) for item in output if item.get("type") == "message").strip()
        if index is None:
            index = next((i for i, item in enumerate(self.calls) if item.get("name") not in READS), 0)
        self.index = index
        call = self.calls[index] if self.calls else None
        self.tool = call["name"] if call else None
        self.call_id = call.get("call_id") if call else None
        self.arguments = self.parsed(call) if call else {}
        self.problem = self.invalid() if call else ""

    @staticmethod
    def parsed(call):
        try:
            return json.loads(call.get("arguments") or "{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return {"(unreadable)": call.get("arguments")}

    def each_read(self):
        """A step for every call of a response with no change in it, in the
        order the model wrote them."""
        return [Step(self.output, index) for index in range(len(self.calls))]

    def invalid(self):
        """Arguments the registry would refuse, as far as the schema says. The
        refusal is not this suite's to test; it is reported beside the call."""
        schema = next((tool["parameters"] for tool in TOOLS if tool["name"] == self.tool), None)
        if schema is None:
            return "unknown tool"
        missing = [name for name in schema.get("required", []) if name not in self.arguments]
        extra = [name for name in self.arguments if name not in schema.get("properties", {})]
        return f"invalid arguments: missing {missing}, unexpected {extra}" if missing or extra else ""

    def keys(self):
        """The settings a settings call names."""
        return set(self.arguments.get("keys") or []) | set(self.arguments.get("changes") or {})

    def changes(self):
        return self.tool is not None and self.tool not in READS

    def reads(self):
        return self.tool in READS

    def __str__(self):
        if not self.tool:
            return "reply: " + (self.reply.replace("\n", " ")[:160] or "(empty)")
        text = f"{self.tool} {json.dumps(self.arguments, ensure_ascii=False)}" + (f" ({self.problem})" if self.problem else "")
        others = [f"{call['name']} {json.dumps(self.parsed(call), ensure_ascii=False)}"
                  for index, call in enumerate(self.calls) if index != self.index]
        return text + (f" [same response: {'; '.join(others)}]" if others else "")


# --- Cases -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Each case names its request in requests.json and, in its docstring, the
# sentence of projectInstructions.ts it tests (line numbers at 6b4b8b6188).
# check() returns PASS, FAIL, UNOBSERVED or CONTINUE with a detail. CONTINUE
# is a read the case does not decide on: when it decides on none of a
# response's reads, the runner answers them all from the recording and asks
# again. UNOBSERVED is a step the case can say nothing about, or a read with
# no recorded answer, or the model still reading after MAX_READS answers.


def run_steps(name, respond, deliver=lambda step, results: None):
    """One run of a case: respond(input) is the model's output for the
    request so far, deliver(step, results) hands it its reads' results."""
    input = list(REQUESTS[name]["body"]["input"])
    # The recorded request's last items that the app sends on it alone (a
    # skill and its picture): a continuation of the turn leaves them out.
    once = REQUESTS[name].get("once", 0)
    path = []  # the reads answered, one entry per response, for the report
    try:
        for _ in range(MAX_READS + 1):
            log = [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]
            step = Step(respond(input))
            verdict, detail = judge_response(CASES[name](REQUESTS[name], log), step)
            if verdict != CONTINUE:
                break
            results, missing = answers_for(name, step)
            if results is None or len(path) == MAX_READS:
                verdict = UNOBSERVED
                detail = (f"no recorded answer for {missing}" if results is None else f"still reading after answers: {step}")
                break
            path.append(" + ".join(call["name"] for call in step.calls))
            deliver(step, results)
            # As the app continues a turn: the history without what was sent
            # once, the model's output, then a result for every call, in the
            # order the calls were written.
            if once:
                del input[-once:]
                once = 0
            input += step.output + [{"type": "function_call_output", "call_id": call.get("call_id"), "output": result}
                                    for call, result in zip(step.calls, results)]
    except Exception as error:  # a failed request is a failed run, reported as such
        return FAIL, f"ERROR {error}", [line for line in map(readable, input) if line]
    prefix = f"after {', '.join(path)}: " if path else ""
    return verdict, prefix + detail, log + ["model: " + str(step)] + (["model said: " + step.reply] if step.reply and step.tool else [])

content.text:
Confirmed on both counts. The prompt-test runner answers reads that the app would refuse, and it has done so since the suite's first commit (5ae439525b, 2026-10-15), well before the subscription backend. I changed nothing.

**What happens.** When the model asks for a read, the runner (`tests/project_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`) checks the arguments against the tool's schema. `Step.invalid()` produces messages like "unexpected ['sessionId']" or "missing ['query']" into `Step.problem`. But that value is only used when the step is printed (line 284). The code that picks the recorded answer (`answers_for` and `recorded_answer`) never looks at it, so the read gets the recorded "succeeded" result anyway.

The app refuses the same call. `ToolRegistry::validate_call` rejects it with "Not a parameter of this tool: …", because the tool schemas set `additionalProperties: false`. The model would get a refusal back, not the data. The README says the opposite of what the code does: "A call with arguments the registry would refuse is never answered either". That sentence dates from the same first commit.

**Reproduced offline** (no model calls), with a recorded `settings_search` from `model-opened-unnamed`:

| Call | Runner's own check | Answered? |
|---|---|---|
| Valid arguments | (none) | yes, succeeded |
| Extra `sessionId` | unexpected ['sessionId'] | yes, succeeded |
| Missing required `query` | missing ['query'] | yes, succeeded |

**It predates the subscription backend.** I ran the same reproduction against the runner as it was at 170d1ae080, the commit just before the backend:
- The extra-`sessionId` call was answered there too.
- The missing-`query` call was answered too, once the runner had a recorded search with an empty query. Those recordings only arrived with 3341abf38f, so that variant can now come up in practice, but the matching code that answers it is the same old code.

**Effect on results: unknown.** The other session saw it happen once (`model-opened-unnamed`, run 2). Today's baseline log shows no "invalid arguments" lines, but that doesn't clear it: the log shows the arguments only for each run's final step, and earlier answered reads appear by tool name alone. So I can't say whether any of today's 69 passes went through an invalid read.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The claude-cli backend against a fake Messages endpoint: what the model
would receive, and the step rules through real MCP calls. Runs the installed
Claude Code CLI with a dummy API key aimed at a local server, so it needs no
login, sends nothing anywhere and costs nothing. Skipped when `claude` is not
on PATH. Run it after a CLI update: the resumed session is the CLI's own
internal format.

Usage: python3 tests/project_prompt/test_claude_cli.py
"""

import http.server
import importlib.util
import json
import os
import pathlib
import shutil
import threading
import unittest

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("run_prompt_tests", HERE / "run_prompt_tests.py")
runner = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(runner)
cli = runner.claude_cli


class FakeMessages:
    """Answers each streamed request with the next scripted response (a list
    of content blocks) and keeps every request body."""

    def __init__(self, *responses):
        self.responses, self.bodies = list(responses), []
        fake = self

        class Handler(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
            def log_message(self, *_):
                pass

            def do_HEAD(self):
                self.send_response(200)
                self.end_headers()

            def do_POST(self):
                body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(int(self.headers.get("content-length", 0))))
                if not self.path.startswith("/v1/messages") or "count_tokens" in self.path or not body.get("stream"):
                    self.send_response(404)
                    self.end_headers()
                    return
                fake.bodies.append(body)
                blocks = fake.responses.pop(0) if fake.responses else [{"type": "text", "text": "(nothing scripted)"}]
                self.send_response(200)
                self.send_header("content-type", "text/event-stream")
                self.end_headers()

                def event(data):
                    self.wfile.write(f"event: {data['type']}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n".encode())

                event({"type": "message_start", "message": {"id": f"msg_{len(fake.bodies)}", "type": "message",
                       "role": "assistant", "model": body["model"], "content": [], "stop_reason": None,
                       "usage": {"input_tokens": 10, "output_tokens": 1}}})
                for index, block in enumerate(blocks):
                    if block["type"] == "text":
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block": {"type": "text", "text": ""}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "text_delta", "text": block["text"]}})
                    else:
                        event({"type": "content_block_start", "index": index, "content_block":
                               {"type": "tool_use", "id": f"toolu_{len(fake.bodies)}_{index}", "name": block["name"],
                                "input": {}}})
                        event({"type": "content_block_delta", "index": index,
                               "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(block["input"])}})
                    event({"type": "content_block_stop", "index": index})
                stop = "tool_use" if any(block["type"] == "tool_use" for block in blocks) else "end_turn"
                event({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": stop, "stop_sequence": None},
                       "usage": {"output_tokens": 5}})
                event({"type": "message_stop"})

        self.server = http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server.server_address[1]}"

    def close(self):
        self.server.shutdown()
        self.server.server_close()


def tool(name, arguments):
    return {"type": "tool_use", "name": cli.PREFIX + name, "input": arguments}


def plain(value):
    """A request's content without the CLI's cache markers."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [plain(item) for item in value]
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {key: plain(item) for key, item in value.items() if key != "cache_control"}
    return value


def conversation(body):
    """A request's messages without the CLI's own system turns (its
    environment note, and an empty one carrying the effort setting)."""
    return [message for message in plain(body["messages"]) if message["role"] != "system"]

Refuse a model's call in the prompt runner exactly as the app does

The runner answered a read from the recording even when the app would
refuse its arguments: Step.problem, a schema-only guess at the refusal, was
only printed. On 2026-10-20 a settings_search with a sessionId it does not
take was answered in model-opened-unnamed. The gap was there from the
suite's first commit (5ae439525b), the README said the opposite ("never
answered"), and several test_steps.py cases scripted such calls themselves
(scope "print", slice_start {"wait": true}, an empty patch).

The app's input check is not the schema: ToolRegistry::validate_call runs
valid_arguments, about 620 lines of rules per tool (scope and target, limit
1 to 25, section names, ...). Rather than a second copy in Python, the new
tests/agent/tool_call_check builds ToolRegistry.cpp and ToolResults.cpp into
a small GUI-free command that answers each call with validate_call's own
code and message. The runner uses the newest one under build/ (or
JUSPRIN_TOOL_CALL_CHECK) and stops when it is older than ToolRegistry.cpp.

As ProviderAgent::next_call does, a response's calls run in order: the first
one not offered on the request (unknown_tool) or not accepted gets the app's
refusal as its result, every later call is answered "not run", and the run
goes on. Two refusals a run are answered; the third fails it
(malformed_tool_call). A refused call is never judged, read or change: the
case sees only the calls before it. recorded_answer's special case for a
non-object target goes, since the refusal now covers it.

Tests: test_steps.py gains eight cases (a refused read, a rule beyond the
schema, a tool not offered, not_run after a refusal, a refused change and a
change after a refused read never judged, the third refusal, and the
refusal words read from ProviderAgent.cpp); all eight fail on the old
runner. test_claude_cli.py gains the refusal reaching the model through the
stub (fails on the old runner). The five existing cases that scripted
